reason: The beds need a supporting structure on the growing-room floor before they can be lined.
expectation: The steel will form a bed frame on the floor.

effect: The steel created raised frames with outlets above the future reservoir; they are ready to be lined.
reaction: The distinct bed shapes make the crop plan clearer.
reason: The food-safe sheet should line the newly built bed frames.
expectation: The sheet will line the shared bed structure.

effect: The lined beds have open drain stubs, so the next task is connecting them to the reservoir.
reaction: The description makes the remaining plumbing clear.
reason: The service hose should connect the bed drains to the reservoir system.
expectation: The hose will connect the drains or prepare them for connection to the reservoir.

effect: The bed drains now join into a common outlet, but the reservoir still needs mounting beneath it.
reason: The reservoir and pump belong beneath the loose drain outlet.
expectation: The reservoir will be mounted and connected to the common drain.

effect: The reservoir and pump completed the recirculating bed system, with falling return water providing aeration.
reaction: The simple use of the return-water drop to mix in oxygen was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the reservoir was most worthwhile: it completed the system and explained how the shared pump and aerated return work.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the drain hoses was a clear but fairly routine intermediate step.

surprise.text: I hadn't anticipated that the return water would fall through air to mix in oxygen without another machine.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the frames, liner, hoses and reservoir each had a clear physical purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I'd be curious to see how the empty beds become a working food system; the plumbing made this chapter feel physically grounded.
